userStories.title: Add categoryToFixTarget SSOT helper and review export
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a single SSOT helper that maps adversarial categories to `fixTarget` without duplicating the blocking-category list.

**Motivation** — The signal exists; it is simply not populated for adversarial findings (only `test-gap → "test"` today, `adversarial-helpers.ts:108`) and is overridden by the test-writer's blanket clause.

**Approach** — `categoryToFixTarget(category)` is a pure, deterministic map (not an LLM call), backed by `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES`:

| category | fixTarget | rationale |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `input`, `error-path`, `abandonment`, `assumption` | `"source"` | the `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES` source-defect set |
| `test-gap` | `"test"` | test quality — the test-writer's lane |
| `convention` | `"test"` | conservative: stays on the test-writer (ambiguous bucket, never routed to un-reviewed source) |
| unrecognized | `"test"` | safe default — never route an unknown category to source editing |

### Worked skeleton — `categoryToFixTarget` (novel SSOT helper)

```typescript
// src/review/category-fix-target.ts
import { BLOCKING_CATEGORIES } from "./ac-structural-counterfactual";
import type { FixTarget } from "../findings/types";

/**
 * Maps an adversarial finding category to the fix lane that owns it.
 * SSOT: the "source" set IS `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES` — never a hand-copied list.
 * `convention` and any unrecognized category default to "test" (conservative:
 * the implementer never receives an ambiguous/unknown finding for un-reviewed
 * source editing).
 */
export function categoryToFixTarget(category: string | undefined): FixTarget {
  return category != null && BLOCKING_CATEGORIES.has(category) ? "source" : "test";
}
```

**Scope** — In: `src/review/category-fix-target.ts`, export wiring in `src/review/index.ts`, and unit coverage proving the helper derives source categories from `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES`. Out: converter changes, config/schema changes, routing changes, and diff-cap enforcement.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function categoryToFixTarget(category: string | undefined): FixTarget
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `categoryToFixTarget` imported from `@/review`, when it is called with `"abandonment"`, then it returns `"source"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"input"`, then it returns `"source"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"error-path"`, then it returns `"source"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"assumption"`, then it returns `"source"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"test-gap"`, then it returns `"test"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"convention"`, then it returns `"test"`
Given `categoryToFixTarget`, when it is called with `"some-unrecognized-category"`, then it returns `"test"`

Given every member of `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES`, when `categoryToFixTarget(member)` is evaluated, then it returns `"source"`, and given `"test-gap"` and `"convention"`, when each is evaluated, then it returns `"test"`

routing.reasoning: This is one new pure helper plus one export in an existing module, with direct unit assertions and no integration branching.

userStories.title: Tag adversarial findings with fixTarget and persist it in review audit output
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Populate `fixTarget` consistently on adversarial findings in both the cycle-facing and audit-facing converter paths.

**Motivation** — The per-finding `fixTarget` never governs routing.

**Approach** — `ReviewFinding` — `src/plugins/extensions.ts:20` | `{ ruleId, severity, file, line, message, category?, source?, meta? }` — **no `fixTarget`** | **modify** — add optional `fixTarget?: FixTarget` (additive; plugin-facing)

`toAdversarialReviewFindings` — `src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:94` | sets `fixTarget: f.category === "test-gap" ? "test" : undefined` | **modify** — replace with `categoryToFixTarget(f.category)`

`llmFindingsToReviewFindings` / `llmFindingToReviewFinding` — `src/review/finding-projection.ts:104,121` | builds `ReviewFinding`, does **not** set `fixTarget` | **modify** — set `fixTarget` via the same map (feeds the audit)

`ReviewAuditEntry.result.findings` — `src/review/review-audit.ts:58` | `{ passed: boolean; findings: unknown[] } | null` | **read** — no schema change; `fixTarget` rides through `unknown[]` once `ReviewFinding` carries it |

**Scope** — In: adversarial finding conversion, review finding projection, plugin-facing `ReviewFinding` typing, and audit persistence coverage. Out: strategy predicates, config scope changes, and diff-cap logic.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface ReviewFinding {
  fixTarget?: FixTarget;
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given an adversarial LLM finding with `category: "abandonment"`, when `toAdversarialReviewFindings` converts it, then the returned `Finding.fixTarget` equals `"source"`
Given an adversarial LLM finding with `category: "test-gap"`, when `toAdversarialReviewFindings` converts it, then the returned `Finding.fixTarget` equals `"test"`

Given an adversarial LLM finding with `category: "input"`, when `llmFindingsToReviewFindings` converts it with `source: "adversarial-review"`, then the returned `ReviewFinding.fixTarget` equals `"source"`
Given the same adversarial LLM finding, when it is converted through `toAdversarialReviewFindings` and `llmFindingsToReviewFindings`, then both outputs carry the same `fixTarget` value
Given an adversarial LLM finding with `category: "some-unrecognized-category"`, when it is converted through `llmFindingsToReviewFindings`, then the returned `ReviewFinding.fixTarget` equals `"test"`

Given an adversarial review-audit entry recorded for a finding with `category: "abandonment"`, when the corresponding `ReviewAuditEntry` is persisted, then the stored finding carries `fixTarget: "source"`

routing.reasoning: The change is spread across two existing converter paths and an additive interface field, but it stays inside established review-mapping code and current audit tests.

userStories.title: Add triage scope to non-blocking config and verifier guard wiring
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the non-blocking fix configuration to expose `scope: "triage"`, keep `both` as the default, and make verifier guarding apply to triage-capable test edits.

**Motivation** — Default stays `both`; `triage` is opt-in.

**Approach** — `nonBlockingFix` schema — `src/config/schemas-review.ts:129` | `scope: z.enum(["source","both"]).default("both")` | **modify** — add `"triage"`; add `sourceDiffCap`

`NonBlockingFixConfig` — `src/config/selectors.ts:143` | derived from schema | **read** — type updates automatically |

`nonBlockingExtraPhases` — `src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts` | `cfg.scope === "both" && cfg.verifierGuard ? ["verifier"] : []` | **modify** — apply verifier guard under `"triage"` too |

**Scope** — In: schema/defaults for `scope`, invalid-scope rejection, and `nonBlockingExtraPhases()` behavior for triage. Out: strategy routing changes and diff-cap enforcement internals.

**Interface**
```typescript
scope: z.enum(["source", "both", "triage"]).default("both")
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema`, when it parses `{ nonBlockingFix: { enabled: true, scope: "triage" } }`, then the parsed `nonBlockingFix.scope` equals `"triage"`
Given `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema`, when it parses a `nonBlockingFix` object with `scope` unset, then the parsed `nonBlockingFix.scope` equals `"both"`
Given `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema`, when it parses `{ nonBlockingFix: { enabled: true, scope: "invalid" } }`, then parsing throws
Given `nonBlockingExtraPhases`, when it is called with `{ scope: "triage", verifierGuard: true, ... }`, then it returns `["verifier"]`
Given `nonBlockingExtraPhases`, when it is called with `{ scope: "triage", verifierGuard: false, ... }`, then it returns `[]`

routing.reasoning: This is a schema enum expansion plus one pure revalidation helper change, using the repo’s established config pattern and existing unit-test seams.

userStories.title: Build the triage strategy set with default-preserving implementer and test-writer options
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a dedicated `triage` non-blocking strategy branch that routes each adversarial finding by `fixTarget` while preserving current behavior everywhere else.

**Motivation** — The fix is to route by category.

**Approach** — Routing under `scope: "triage"`: the implementer claims `fixTarget === "source"` adversarial findings; the test-writer claims `fixTarget === "test"` adversarial findings; `full-suite-rectify` recovers regressions — exactly one strategy claims each finding.

`nbf strategy build — src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:234-258` | `source`/`both` branches | **modify** — add `triage` branch |

`makeAutofixTestWriterStrategy` — `src/operations/autofix-test-writer-strategy.ts:11` | `(story, config, sink)`, `appliesTo` claims all adversarial | **modify** — add default-preserving options object; option to disable the blanket adversarial clause |

`makeAutofixImplementerStrategy` — `src/operations/autofix-implementer-strategy.ts:27` | `(story, config, sink, { includeAdversarialReview? })` | **modify** — option to claim `fixTarget === "source"` adversarial findings |

Pattern to mirror: the existing `source`/`both` branches in `build-plan-for-strategy.ts:234-258` already build scope-specific strategy sets with a private `nbSink` and `nbPostValidate` — the `triage` branch follows the same shape. Default-preserving factory options follow `makeAutofixImplementerStrategy`'s existing `AutofixImplementerStrategyOptions` pattern (`autofix-implementer-strategy.ts:13-25`).

**Scope** — In: non-blocking `triage` branch, strategy predicate options, and proof that blocking and existing default branches remain unchanged. Out: category mapping logic and diff-cap enforcement.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface AutofixImplementerStrategyOptions {
  includeAdversarialReview?: boolean;
}
```
```typescript
export function makeAutofixImplementerStrategy(
  story: UserStory,
  config: NaxConfig,
  sink: DeclarationSink,
  opts: AutofixImplementerStrategyOptions = {},
): FixStrategy<Finding, AutofixImplementerInput, AutofixImplementerOutput, AutofixConfig>
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given the non-blocking strategy set built for `scope: "triage"`, when the strategy names are inspected, then they include `"autofix-implementer"`, `"autofix-test-writer"`, and `"full-suite-rectify"`

Given the `triage` strategy set and an advisory finding with `source: "adversarial-review"` and `fixTarget: "source"`, when each strategy's `appliesTo` is evaluated, then `autofix-implementer` returns `true` and `autofix-test-writer` returns `false`

Given the `triage` strategy set and an advisory finding with `source: "adversarial-review"` and `fixTarget: "test"`, when each strategy's `appliesTo` is evaluated, then `autofix-test-writer` returns `true` and `autofix-implementer` returns `false`
Given the `triage` strategy set and an advisory `convention` finding with `fixTarget: "test"`, when `autofix-test-writer.appliesTo` is evaluated, then it returns `true`
Given `makeAutofixTestWriterStrategy` built with default options, when `appliesTo` is evaluated for an adversarial finding with `fixTarget: "source"`, then it returns `true`

Given the blocking three-session strategy set, when an adversarial finding with `fixTarget: "source"` is evaluated, then `autofix-test-writer.appliesTo` returns `true` and `autofix-implementer.appliesTo` returns `false`

routing.reasoning: This is a four-file behavior change built on existing strategy factories and unit tests, with explicit backward-compatibility assertions already defined by the spec.

userStories.title: Enforce source-edit diff caps with restore-over-keep in runNonBlockingFix
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Bound the source-edit surface that triage enables by measuring non-test source edits and restoring the snapshot when the cap is exceeded or cannot be measured.

**Motivation** — A minimal `sourceDiffCap` bounds the un-reviewed source edits that triage newly enables.

**Approach** — `runNonBlockingFix` / `NonBlockingFixDeps` — `src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:62` | `_deps = { captureSnapshotRef, rollbackToRef }` | **modify** — add `measureSourceDiff` dep; enforce `sourceDiffCap` before keep |

**Failure Handling**
- **Floor unchanged.** Snapshot at pass entry → restore files + `phaseOutputs` on exhaustion (`non-blocking-fix.ts:73,93-98`). Worst case remains "nothing changed."
- **Source-diff over cap → restore-over-keep.** A best-effort pass whose **source** diff (test files excluded via `resolveTestFilePatterns`, never an inline regex) exceeds `sourceDiffCap` is treated as exhausted → restored. This is the only new failure path; it is fail-safe (defaults to restore).
- **Unknown category → `"test"`** (never routed to the implementer).
- **`measureSourceDiff` errors** are treated as "cap exceeded" → restore (fail-safe).

**Scope** — In: non-blocking keep/restore logic, `NonBlockingFixDeps`, config defaults for `sourceDiffCap`, and diff measurement wired through test-file resolution. Out: strategy predicates and audit tagging.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface NonBlockingFixDeps {
  captureSnapshotRef: typeof captureSnapshotRef;
  rollbackToRef: typeof rollbackToRef;
}
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given `AdversarialReviewConfigSchema`, when it parses a `nonBlockingFix` object with `sourceDiffCap` unset, then the parsed `sourceDiffCap.maxFiles` and `sourceDiffCap.maxLines` equal their schema defaults

Given `runNonBlockingFix` with a `measureSourceDiff` dependency reporting a source change that exceeds `sourceDiffCap.maxLines` and a `runRectify` result where `rectificationExhausted` is `false`, when the function completes, then it returns `{ ran: true, kept: false, restored: true }` and invokes the rollback dependency

Given `runNonBlockingFix` with a `measureSourceDiff` dependency reporting a source change within `sourceDiffCap` and a `runRectify` result where `rectificationExhausted` is `false`, when the function completes, then it returns `{ ran: true, kept: true, restored: false }`
Given `runNonBlockingFix` with a `measureSourceDiff` dependency that throws, when the function completes, then it returns `{ ran: true, kept: false, restored: true }`

Given `runNonBlockingFix` with a diff whose changed files are all test files and whose measured source-line count is zero, when the diff stays within `sourceDiffCap`, then it returns `{ ran: true, kept: true, restored: false }`

routing.reasoning: The change extends one existing execution helper and one schema with a fail-safe branch, and the behavior is directly observable through current unit-test seams.

analysis:
The feature is an additive change to the adversarial non-blocking fix path, not a greenfield subsystem. The existing SSOT for source-defect adversarial categories already exists as `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES` in `src/review/ac-structural-counterfactual.ts:25`, and its unit contract is already pinned by `test/unit/review/ac-structural-counterfactual.test.ts:13`. Today adversarial wire findings only tag `fixTarget` for `test-gap`; every other adversarial finding leaves it unset in `src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:94`, specifically `fixTarget: f.category === "test-gap" ? "test" : undefined` at `src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:108`. Audit-side `ReviewFinding` projection also drops `fixTarget` entirely: `llmFindingToReviewFinding()` and `llmFindingsToReviewFindings()` build `ReviewFinding` with category/source/meta only in `src/review/finding-projection.ts:104-122`, while the plugin-facing `ReviewFinding` shape in `src/plugins/extensions.ts:20-50` has no `fixTarget` field. That means triage cannot work until both producer paths agree on the same category-to-target mapping and the audit contract grows an additive optional field.

The routing bug is real in current code. Non-blocking strategy assembly only has `source` and `both` branches in `src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:234-258`. In `scope === "source"`, the implementer is configured with `includeAdversarialReview: true` (`src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:239-245`). In the `else` branch, which is effectively `both`, the implementer is explicitly configured with `includeAdversarialReview: false` and the test-writer is always added (`src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:246-253`). The test-writer then claims every adversarial finding unconditionally because `makeAutofixTestWriterStrategy()` uses `f.fixTarget === "test" || f.source === "adversarial-review" || sink.mockHandoffs.length > 0` in `src/operations/autofix-test-writer-strategy.ts:11-19`. The implementer strategy already has an options-object seam that can be extended without breaking callers: `AutofixImplementerStrategyOptions` lives at `src/operations/autofix-implementer-strategy.ts:13-25`, and the current predicate only claims allowed sources or all adversarial findings when `includeAdversarialReview` is set (`src/operations/autofix-implementer-strategy.ts:27-42`). The cycle contract explicitly expects `appliesTo` to discriminate by `source`, `category`, `fixTarget`, or file pattern in `src/findings/cycle-types.ts:118-122`, so the spec’s triage routing is aligned with the existing architecture rather than a new pattern.

Config and orchestration seams are already isolated. The schema currently restricts `nonBlockingFix.scope` to `"source" | "both"` with `both` defaulting in `src/config/schemas-review.ts:121-139`, and the derived type alias comes from the schema in `src/config/selectors.ts:143`, so adding `triage` and `sourceDiffCap` at the schema automatically updates the public selector type. Runtime behavior for verifier guarding is centralized in `src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:29-32`, where `nonBlockingExtraPhases()` currently returns `["verifier"]` only for `scope === "both" && cfg.verifierGuard`; that is the only place the triage scope must be wired for revalidation behavior. `runNonBlockingFix()` is already the keep-vs-restore boundary, with `_deps` containing only snapshot/rollback hooks in `src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:34-40` and restore semantics implemented at `src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:62-103`. This is the right insertion point for `measureSourceDiff`, the cap decision, and the fail-safe restore path because the function already snapshots files and in-place restores `phaseOutputs` on exhaustion. The test-file SSOT needed for source-only diff counting already exists in `resolveTestFilePatterns()` in `src/test-runners/resolver.ts:1-195`; ADR-009 is explicit that inline test-file checks are forbidden (`src/test-runners/resolver.ts:3-7`), so any diff-cap implementation should reuse that resolver rather than invent a new matcher.

Existing tests give clear extension points. Config defaults and invalid-scope rejection are already covered in `test/unit/config/non-blocking-fix-config.test.ts:5-27`. Non-blocking run gating, keep-vs-restore behavior, and rollback of `phaseOutputs` are already covered in `test/unit/execution/non-blocking-fix.test.ts:8-92` and `test/unit/execution/non-blocking-fix-wiring.test.ts:5-24`. `BLOCKING_CATEGORIES` is pinned by `test/unit/review/ac-structural-counterfactual.test.ts:13-19`. `llmFindingToReviewFinding()` already has focused unit coverage for category, source propagation, and meta shaping in `test/unit/review/finding-projection.test.ts:8-189`, making it the natural place to add `fixTarget` assertions. `toAdversarialReviewFindings()` already has direct unit coverage for metadata passthrough in `test/unit/review/adversarial-metadata-audit.test.ts:353-388`, so extending those tests with `fixTarget` expectations fits the current suite layout. The test-writer’s blanket adversarial behavior is already codified in `test/unit/operations/autofix-test-writer-strategy.test.ts:40-84`, and the implementer’s current refusal to claim `adversarial-review` unless opted in is codified in `test/unit/operations/autofix-implementer-strategy.test.ts:41-117`. Plan assembly already has strategy-capture tests in `test/unit/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.test.ts:578-625`. Review-audit shape for adversarial findings is covered by tests that inspect persisted `ReviewFinding[]` payloads in `test/unit/review/adversarial-audit-shape.test.ts:71-132`, so extending the persisted shape with `fixTarget` is low-risk and observable. Builder storage for non-blocking fix overrides is already covered in `test/unit/execution/rectification-overrides.test.ts:28-47`, which is relevant when adding a new `triage` scope branch.

Impact areas are localized but cross-module: review mapping (`src/review/*`), plugin-facing finding types (`src/plugins/extensions.ts`), config schema/selectors (`src/config/*`), strategy routing (`src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts`, `src/operations/autofix-*-strategy.ts`), and non-blocking restore logic (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts`). Backward compatibility risk is mainly behavioral: `scope: "both"`, `scope: "source"`, and the blocking cycle must remain byte-identical even after adversarial findings start carrying `fixTarget`. The safest way to preserve that is exactly what the spec prescribes: add default-preserving factory options to the strategy builders instead of changing their defaults, and keep the blocking strategy set on the existing blanket test-writer path. The plugin contract change is additive because `ReviewFinding.fixTarget` is optional; existing review plugins will remain valid. Unknown categories must default to `"test"` so new or malformed reviewer categories never unlock unreviewed source edits. The new `sourceDiffCap` is a safety rail, not a migration burden: any cap or measurement failure should restore to the adversarial-passed snapshot instead of partially keeping changes. There is no external migration step; the feature is opt-in through `review.adversarial.nonBlockingFix.scope = "triage"`, with default scope remaining `"both"`.
